errors.description: Direction of the slant relative to the pressed front crease. Render: it starts about 191px from the crease and widens to about 270px - it DIVERGES. Convergence versus divergence relative to a landmark is unaffected by mirroring, so this is a genuine inversion, not a left/right leg difference.

notes:
IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S FINDINGS. Two of the three minors logged last time were not real defects. Normalising to waistband depth - the one landmark readable cleanly in both images - the drawing's slant offset is 0.89 waistband depths and the render's is 0.89; mouth length 4.06 against 4.08; angle from vertical 12.7 against 12.6. The previous round's '3.0 cm against 2.5 specified' and '14.6 cm against 12' were absolute figures derived by assuming a belt loop is 1.3 cm and converting - against a drawing that carries NO dimension callouts. The uncertainty was stated at the time, but the chain was still assumption-to-conversion-to-comparison, and it produced two corrections chasing errors that did not exist.

METHOD RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: when a drawing carries no callouts, measure RATIOS against a landmark visible in both images. Do not manufacture centimetres from an assumed real-world size and then compare them to a label.

The third minor is genuinely unfixed and worse than a near-miss: the mouth runs the WRONG WAY relative to the crease.

UNRESOLVED, and the reason that finding is major rather than critical: it could not be determined whether the vertical line the red marker lands on is the pressed front crease or the fly/centre-front edge. The same base illustration is used across this option family and the line's identity is ambiguous. If it is the fly, the render's geometry may be correct and the drawing's marker simply sits at the fly. Menswear convention runs a slant pocket down and OUTBOARD toward the side seam, which is what the render did; the drawing appears to specify the opposite. That conflict needs settling against a clearer drawing before another attempt is spent.
